messages:
maya: Kickoff: designing the fallback "auto-rollout" UX — we need clear scoping (global vs per-region), safe defaults, and a tight audit/playback story. Keep it simple for normal users but powerful for SREs.

chris: Agreed. Top-level idea: three-step UI wizard: 1) scope (global/route/region), 2) policy quick knobs (mode + traffic slider + canary presets), 3) audit & preview. Advanced JSON editor behind a chevron.

linh: Quick knobs should include: mode options (soft_steer, hard_switchover, sampled), fallback_traffic_pct with 3 presets (5, 20, 100), cooldown_seconds, trigger_windows, and a small "sensitivity" toggle (low/normal/high) that maps to sane thresholds.

product_ana: Audit requirements: every automatic decision must log decision_id, policy_version, trigger_snapshot (human summary + raw values), metric_window timestamps, operator_id for manual overrides, and a pointer to the raw metric blob for replay. Customers will want CSV/JSON export and org-level retention settings.

chris: For deterministic replay we must store: metric_bucket_start/end, model_version, policy_snapshot, and rng_seed if routing uses any sampling. That should let us re-evaluate the exact decision offline.

maya: UI: show a compact timeline on the rollout page with colored markers (info/warn/error) and an "explain" panel. Clicking a marker opens an audit drawer with a plain-English reason and a single-click "replay" button. Replay runs in sandbox and returns match/mismatch.

linh: Event schema suggestion (for devs, shown to users as fields): decision_id | policy_version | trigger_reason | trigger_values | input_window | final_action | affected_scope | trace_link. Keep payload <1MB; store blobs in object storage and include link.

product_ana: Safety UX: disallow direct 100% hard switchover from the UI without a documented justification and two-step confirmation. For orgs with strict controls enable MFA or 2-person approval for >50% or hard modes. Record approver ids in the audit.

chris: Oscillation mitigation: UI should surface an "auto-pause" state when flips > N within M minutes and provide a suggested remedy (increase cooldown or widen thresholds). Also show a metric that estimates cost impact of fallback (delta tokens/min and dollars/hr).

maya: Scoping: support inheritance — global defaults that can be overridden per-region/route. The UI should show an inheritance breadcrumb and highlight differences. Provide a one-click "sync to parent" and a diff view.

ops-bot: Example override API for docs (ops-only):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/rollouts/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"decision_id":"auto-1865432100-x","override_action":"route_primary","justification":"prod incident","manual":true}'
```

linh: UX microcopy: visualize what "soft_steer" means: "routes X% of traffic to fallback model while keeping existing sessions sticky for Y sec." And show the math for cooldown/hysteresis on hover.

product_ana: Telemetry names + retention classes: rollout.decision (standard), rollout.replay (debug short-retain), rollout.override (audit long-retain), rollout.oscillation (alert). Expose these as filters in the console logs page.

chris: Next steps: I'll draft the event/telemetry schema PR. Linh, please include size & cost estimates for storing blobs at different sample rates. Maya, write UX acceptance tests (oscillation case, region partial outage, noisy transient). Ops-bot, spin up an RFC stub and link mockups.

ops-bot: RFC stub: go/redwood/rfcs/auto-rollout-safety-ui-2026 (draft created).

maya: Thanks — I'll post mockups and a testing rubric by EOD tomorrow. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
